correctness.rationale: Reconstructed both backward problems with the gate generator acting on columns. For Q's eigenvectors 1,z,conjugate(z), K=sqrt((rI−Q)/D) has eigenvalues k0,k,conjugate(k); e0 has coefficient 1/3 in each mode. For joint resetting the no-reset absorption transform at r is exp(−Kx)K^−1e0/(e0^T K^−1e0), from the two Neumann and one Dirichlet data. Its stationary average gives the stated renewal mean. For position-only resetting the bounded solution is h+exp(−Kx)c; the reflecting conditions force Kc=t e0 and the stationary projection of the equation forces π exp(−Ka)c=−1/r, hence t=−3k0 exp(k0a)/r. The z coefficient of h is −k0 exp((k0−k)a)/(κk). The Dirichlet condition cancels the remaining constant in the difference, giving exactly the stated real part. A fixed block has uniformly positive chance of absorption (reset to a, reach the open gate and hit zero during a reset-free interval), giving uniformly finite means and uniqueness of the bounded backward solution by stopping. Re(k)^2−Im(k)^2=(r+3γ/2)/D>k0² and arg(k) is strictly between −π/12 and 0, so the claimed phase, starting sign, and every simple positive zero follow. The proof never subtracts large simulated means to infer high-index reversals.
residual_risks: The finite matrix/backward-grid diagnostics were not rerun and cannot establish the all-distance statement. The result is about stationary-initialized means, not stochastic ordering or arbitrary gate generators.

value.rationale: This gives an explicit counterexample to extrapolating the familiar two-state ordering to a natural nonreversible gate. At every positive rate triple the exact formula specifies which protocol to choose at any given distance and why the advantage can alternate even when the absolute difference is exponentially small. The repeated changes, not merely evaluation of one mean, are the substantive phenomenon.
residual_risks: No experimental resolution of the small large-distance effects, extension to arbitrary switching, or distribution-level dominance is established.
